Automation systems

Chapter 01Local automation · Human approval
The friction

Speed without surrendering judgment.

Job search is repetitive, but the costly actions are irreversible. The system separates preparation from execution, traces every claim to the profile, and makes consent part of the architecture.

The intervention

Research. Tailor. Review. Approve.

Ingest the truth. Then Scan and deduplicate

The outcome

Career Autopilot

0 auto-sends

· every outbound action needs a click

Watch the full story →
approval lever
Chapter 02Personal AI · Offline encrypted
The friction

Useful memory without exporting a life.

A personal assistant becomes more useful as it remembers more — and more dangerous if that memory leaves the machine. LifeOS keeps retrieval, speech, vision and files local while making every tool action inspectable.

The intervention

Unlock only what the task needs.

Unlock locally. Then Retrieve with citations

The outcome

LifeOS

100% offline

· encrypted vault · local models

Watch the full story →
closing shutters
Chapter 03Document automation · Bilingual
The friction

Bilingual should not mean two drifting files.

Company, division and product material arrived in mixed formats. The system extracts sources, normalizes approved content once, and renders both reading directions from the same facts.

The intervention

Source to press-ready, with gates.

Ingest sources. Then Normalize once

The outcome

Medmac Document Studio

5 finished docs

· 22–24 pages each · PDF/X-4

Watch the full story →
press impression
Chapter 04Parametric packaging · Arabic first
The friction

A pretty mockup is not a printable package.

Artwork, folds, panels and printer dimensions often live in separate tools. This system keeps them connected so the visual decision and manufacturing surface cannot silently diverge.

The intervention

Parameter to panel to press.

Choose geometry. Then Art-direct in Arabic

The outcome

Medmac Box Studio

117 checks

· 36 controls · 0.000% layout drift

Watch the full story →
carton fold
Chapter 05Production system · Arabic first
The friction

The design has to survive the kitchen.

A render is not enough for production. The system preserves dimensions, Arabic text, decoration choices and order facts in one CakeDocument with 17 slots, then derives every downstream artifact.

The intervention

Design and production share the same object.

Capture the order. Then Compose the design

The outcome

Cake Studio

588 tests

· 17-slot document · web + desktop

Watch the full story →
icing reveal
Chapter 06Internal tools · LAN security
The friction

A shared folder has no accountable reader.

The risk was not only unauthorized access; it was copying, bulk pulling and losing the trail. The replacement scopes every query by owner and designs revocation, watermarking and audit integrity into the data path.

The intervention

Import safely. Serve minimally. Record permanently.

Checksum the archive. Then Scope by owner

The outcome

MEDMACK Quotations Locker

LAN only

· 128-bit ids · append-only audit

Watch the full story →
vault seal
Chapter 07Windows systems · NTFS
The friction

NTFS already knows where every file is.

A directory walk pays per file. The MFT stores names, parents, sizes and attributes in a mostly contiguous index, so Reclaim turns millions of scattered calls into a sequential parse.

The intervention

Fast discovery, slow authority.

Discover the MFT. Then Stream and roll up

The outcome

Reclaim

4–12 s

· 1.86 TB · 2.6M files · measured

Watch the full story →
shelf rush
Chapter 08Operations · Linear programming
The friction

The ideal ration is useless if the feed is not there.

The solver starts with actual kilograms on hand, protects hard availability and intake limits, then reports nutrient shortfalls instead of failing or pretending every target can be met.

The intervention

Track the stage. Solve the ration. Explain the gap.

Move through the cycle. Then Surface overdue cases

The outcome

Sheep Cycle

76 checks

· 26 logic + 50 UI · offline

Watch the full story →
balance drop
Chapter 09Document tooling · Claude skill
The friction

“Looks like two pages” is not a measurement.

Word layout changes with fonts, spacing and the renderer. The skill treats page count as an observed result, scales typography and spacing together, and warns instead of hiding an impossible fit.

The intervention

Render, count, search, verify.

Load one record. Then Build DOCX

The outcome

Resume Builder Skill

4 layouts

· exact 1- or 2-page fitting

Watch the full story →
page measure
Chapter 10Simulation architecture · Godot
The friction

Do not bake authority into presentation.

Even offline, the human and bots submit the same intent schema. That keeps hit detection, damage and rules in one layer and leaves a clean seam for future transport.

The intervention

Intent in. State and events out.

Capture intent. Then Tick authority

The outcome

Polyblast Arena

60 Hz

· authoritative sim · ~90 checks

Watch the full story →
referee tick
Chapter 11Retail operations · Local control plane
The friction

Channels multiply. Operational truth should not.

Orders, stock, appointments, forecasts, alerts, reports, and proof of delivery arrive with different shapes. The hub normalizes those contracts into one inspectable database and one operating view.

The intervention

Ingest. Normalize. Forecast. Act.

Unify channels. Then Reconcile stock

The outcome

PetPoint Ops Hub

1,490 orders

· 4 branches · synthetic demo data

Watch the full story →
branch route
Chapter 12Workflow orchestration · Observable operations
The friction

A green status is not an explanation.

When workflows cross teams and datasets, operators need to know what ran, which rows changed, where a retry happened, what was skipped, and which alert owns the failure.

The intervention

Schedule. Isolate. Observe. Resolve.

Compose a workflow. Then Run with savepoints

The outcome

RelayOps

56 tests

· 4 workflows · deterministic fallback

Watch the full story →
rail switch
Chapter 13Document automation · Local OCR
The friction

A PDF is readable. Operations need rows.

Statements vary between embedded text, scans, shifting columns, and repeated page headers. The tool must preserve real dates and numbers while making uncertainty visible for review.

The intervention

Read. Detect. Structure. Compare.

Read text or pixels. Then Recover the table

The outcome

Statement Styler

2 outputs

· XLSX + A4 PDF · local only

Watch the full story →
scanner pass

Chapter 23Engineering Lab · Structural analysis
The friction

Structural output needs provenance and blockers.

Geometry, loads, supports, solver assumptions, code checks, and fabrication schedules must remain traceable. A plausible viewport is never a construction approval.

The intervention

Model. Solve. Screen. Export.

Author the frame. Then Solve the truss

The outcome

Spaceframe World 2026

2 solvers

· dense LU + sparse PCG · pre-release

Watch the full story →
load deflect
Chapter 24Engineering Lab · Transfer pipeline
The friction

A clean log can still render the wrong face.

Map names, colour spaces, UV layouts, grooms and render lighting can each report success while producing the wrong visual result. The pipeline treats discovery, readback and measurement as separate proof layers.

The intervention

Discover before writing. Verify after.

Export sampled maps. Then Compose by layer

The outcome

B2MH

dE 8.49 → 1.41

· measured texture seam

Watch the full story →
material layer
Chapter 25Engineering Lab · Data-driven rules
The friction

Recovered rules need provenance, not nostalgia.

The project separates verified source behavior, client-side approximations and deliberate deviations inside the data itself, so a mechanic can be inspected without reading it out of presentation code.

The intervention

Cited data feeds one authority.

Label provenance. Then Load at runtime

The outcome

ARTILLERY3D Architecture

503 map records

· runtime JSON · source labels

Watch the full story →
turn referee
Chapter 26Engineering Lab · Unreal architecture
The friction

A repository should not imply what it cannot build.

The working project depended on a large binary Content tree and third-party art. The portfolio therefore presents the authored module, ground-truth record and verification system — not screenshots as evidence of a redistributable game.

The intervention

Gameplay, systems, UI and tests stay legible.

Own combat in GAS. Then Drive content from data

The outcome

War Strikes Architecture

184 tests

· code + docs · no playable claim

Watch the full story →
test wall
Chapter 27Engineering Lab · Software preservation
The friction

Migration is archaeology with a compiler.

The old client carried assumptions about Unity 4-era assets, bootstrap order, shaders, Steam and SOAP services. Restoration means preserving those contracts while clearly separating new patches from original intellectual property.

The intervention

Recover. Migrate. Bridge. Attribute.

Recover the client. Then Restore compatibility

The outcome

UberStrike Unity 6 Reborn

Unity 6

· preservation, not original authorship

Watch the full story →
museum glass
Chapter 28Private case study · Ground-truth audits
The friction

Faithfulness includes recording what is missing.

Reconstruction can quietly turn assumptions into “facts.” This project kept three provenance states load-bearing across mechanics and content, then verified wiring and reachability in the packaged application.

The intervention

Mine, label, wire, prove.

Mine the source. Then Label confidence

The outcome

Cocolani 3D — Sanitized Study

3 truth labels

· VERIFIED · INFERRED · LOST

Watch the full story →
archive fragment
Chapter 29Private case study · Guardrailed operations
The friction

Automation fails when state outruns reality.

A workflow can click a form and still fail to submit, use the wrong identity or invent a value to satisfy validation. The engine makes real data, authorized accounts and recorded evidence prerequisites.

The intervention

Verify identity, execute, capture evidence.

Load verified facts. Then Check the lane

The outcome

Job Apply Engine — Sanitized Study

Evidence first

· staged is not sent

receipt stamp
Chapter 30Engineering Lab · Design systems
The friction

Style should transform without rewriting truth.

The experiments asked how far one verified profile could travel across different visual identities while content, accessibility, performance and bilingual behavior stayed centralized.

The intervention

Content, tokens, motion, platform.

Centralize truth. Then Tokenize identity

The outcome

Portfolio Design System Study

7 worlds

· one content model · three builds
